answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond and build a reputation over a long horizon. A public randomness beacon then assigns agents to small, unpredictable audit groups, so one operator cannot choose only friendly peers. If many identities coordinate, their shared timing, payment paths, or reports reveal the cluster and trigger collective slashing. The attacker must fund every fake identity, wait to earn trust, and risk losing all collateral, making a velvet swarm expensive.
